body:
On my Mali g-71 mp2 with vulkan api 1.0.47 crashed immediately after loading the project. Previously I used Godot engine 4.4.1 stable (play store) runs very well, after updating to 4.5.1 stable it crashed immediately, so on with version 4.6.

Device: Oppo A83 SDK 25, Mali g-71 mp2, opengles 3.2, vulkan api 1.0.47.

Build information: Godot v4.6.stable - Android (SDK 25 build 1599151965) - Single-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL ES 3 (Compatibility) - Mali-G71 - (8 threads)
Do you get a crash stacktrace in `adb logcat`? It would be helpful to confirm whether what you see is the same bug or another Mali related crash.

Thanks, that's helpful. Can you confirm whether there is any stack trace after `--------- beginning of crash`?
It typically starts with `*** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** ***` and doesn't use the `godot` prefix but maybe `DEBUG`.

I've managed to decode the backtrace and gather more context. Here is the breakdown of the crash:
Backtrace Analysis:
```
********** Crash dump: **********
#06 0x0000000000763e48 /system/vendor/lib64/egl/libGLES_mali.so (vkCreateGraphicsPipelines+392)
#07 0x000000000122a8a0 /data/app/org.godotengine.editor.v4-1/lib/arm64/libgodot_android.so (offset 0x3aea000) 


I decoded (0122a8a0):

 _doc_data_compressed
editor_help.cpp:0
```

 The crash might be triggered during the editor documentation/help loading (editor_help.cpp).
 It leads to a SIGSEGV inside the mali driver during vkCreateGraphicsPipelines.
Before the crash, the log shows a loop of vkCreateComputePipelines failed with error -3 because the driver vulkan 1.0.47 on mali-g71 doesn't support R8_Uint as a storage image.
It appears that the engine's attempt to repeatedly create pipelines after the initial failure combined with the resource-heavy task of decompressing and rendering editor help eventually causes the driver to dereference a null pointer (fault addr 0x34).

Full log:
